handback.t:
BENCHMARK BUILDER: final report (held-out seeds 31-60 are the honest numbers)

Summary: on held-out seeds, every tuned mesh beats keyword routing, Thompson and its own bare Hebbian leader, with 95% CIs that exclude 0. The gain over the leader is small (about +2 points of success) and comes almost entirely from team tasks. Untuned meshes and the default Hebbian router do not beat keyword routing.

All 43 tests pass under `cargo test --release`. That includes 14 I wrote for sim and stats; the stats tests check against hand-computed values. The full experiment takes about 4 s in release. Nothing is committed, and I did not edit mesh.rs or variants.rs. No API was missing: I used `with_trust_edges` as-is. Fragility over time is not reported; I skipped it to finish on time.

FILES
- C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh\src\sim.rs: the seeded world.
- C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh\src\stats.rs: mean, sample sd, 95% t-interval (t table for df 1-100, 1.96 above that), and paired differences with wins/losses/ties.
- C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh\src\bin\experiment.rs: the runner.
- C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh\results\results.json: tuning grids, per-seed results, summaries, paired diffs, ablations, timings.
- C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh\results\experiment_output.txt: full printed output.

HOW THE WORLD IS BUILT
- Size: 6 named agents, 8 task types, 2000 tasks per run. The best agent for each type succeeds 80-88% of the time.
- Traps (keyword map points to the wrong agent):
  - bugfix: map says coder (0.45), tester is best (0.80).
  - performance: map says architect (0.42), coder is best (0.80).
- Features: 2-3 keywords from the task's own type, plus a 25% chance of one keyword from another type, in shuffled order. Routers do not see the task type unless a run says so (`reveal_type`).
- Drift at task 1000:
  - feature: coder drops 0.85 -> 0.62, architect rises to 0.86.
  - code-review: reviewer drops 0.82 -> 0.60, security-auditor rises to 0.84.
- Team tasks (30% of tasks): success = leader skill + sum of hidden pair synergies, capped to [0.02, 0.97].
  - coder+tester and architect+security-auditor add +0.22; reviewer+docs-writer adds +0.18; every other pair costs -0.06.
  - On solo tasks only the leader's outcome counts, and feedback goes only to the team that actually worked.
- Failure window: one random agent always fails for 200 tasks, placed somewhere in tasks 300-1700.
- Pairing: one uniform random number is pre-drawn per task, so every router sees the same tasks and outcomes for a given seed.
- Regret: the best achievable success probability (best agent, or best team of up to 3) minus that of the team actually used.
- Windows: pre-drift is tasks 0-999, early-post is 1000-1499, late-post is 1500-1999.

TUNING (seeds 1-8 only)
- Hebbian: eta 0.05, temperature 0.02, decay 0.001. Caveat: eta is at the lowest value on the grid, and the tuning-seed score of .752 fell to .734 on held-out seeds.
- Co-activation mesh: edge_eta 0.2, edge_decay 0.01, team_size 2.
- NeuralMesh with `with_trust_edges`: mu 0.25, psi 0.05, team_size 2.
- PgActor: eta 1.0, theta_clip 4.
- R-STDP: eta 0.5, temperature 0.1, tau_e 1.
- trust-mesh-tuned (my own TrustEdges helper wrapper; no health/benching, 5% helper exploration): mu 0.25, psi 0.05, team_size 3.

RESULTS, HELD-OUT SEEDS 31-60 (success ±95% CI | regret | pre / early / late | failure window | team / solo | ns per route; timings vary about ±15% between runs)
- keyword            .6995±.0032 | .169 | .722/.673/.681 | .598 | .699/.700 | 132
- thompson           .6080±.0063 | .260 | .558/.636/.679 | .538 | .610/.607 | 519
- hebbian            .6927±.0117 | .178 | .694/.684/.700 | .649 | .695/.692 | 609
- hebbian-no-decay   .6921±.0127 | .177 | .693/.681/.701 | .660 | .693/.691 | 657
- hebbian-tuned      .7341±.0124 | .136 | .729/.724/.756 | .676 | .738/.732 | ~600
- mesh-k1-hebbian    .7017±.0115 | .167 | .692/.695/.729 | .649 | .706/.700 | 850
- mesh-k2-hebbian    .7190±.0110 | .150 | .705/.717/.748 | .673 | .773/.696 | 1062
- mesh-k3-hebbian    .7159±.0119 | .153 | .701/.707/.754 | .671 | .764/.695 | 1247
- mesh-k2-thompson   .6378±.0053 | .231 | .585/.669/.713 | .579 | .697/.612 | 779
- mesh-k3-thompson   .6298±.0064 | .241 | .579/.657/.705 | .573 | .673/.612 | 797
- mesh-tuned (k2)    .7526±.0124 | .116 | .726/.760/.797 | .688 | .814/.726 | ~1200
- mesh-tuned-k1      .7406±.0082 | .130 | .724/.738/.777 | .691 | .744/.739 | 949
- mesh-k2-trust      .7043±.0126 | .164 | .692/.705/.727 | .679 | .758/.681 | 889
- mesh-k3-trust      .7063±.0131 | .164 | .693/.703/.737 | .659 | .758/.684 | 957
- mesh-trust-tuned   .7543±.0102 | .116 | .727/.766/.797 | .702 | .809/.731 | 956
- trust-mesh-tuned   .7584±.0066 | .110 | .748/.758/.780 | .683 | .816/.734 | ~900
- pg-actor-tuned     .7127±.0071 | .157 | .692/.720/.748 | .635 | .717/.711 | 556
- r-stdp-tuned       .7349±.0070 | .135 | .713/.739/.776 | .670 | .737/.734 | 395
- Untuned: pg-actor .6944, r-stdp .7020.

PAIRED SUCCESS DIFFERENCES, HELD-OUT (significant = CI excludes 0)
- Vs keyword, significantly better:
  - trust-mesh-tuned +.059 (30/30 seeds won)
  - mesh-trust-tuned +.055 (29/30)
  - mesh-tuned +.053 (28/30)
  - mesh-tuned-k1 +.041
  - r-stdp-tuned +.035
  - hebbian-tuned +.035
  - mesh-k2 +.020
  - mesh-k3 +.016
  - pg-actor-tuned +.013
- Vs keyword, not significant: default hebbian (-.007), hebbian-no-decay, mesh-k1, mesh-k2-trust (+.005), mesh-k3-trust (+.007), r-stdp untuned.
- Vs keyword, significantly worse: thompson (-.092), mesh-k2-thompson (-.062), mesh-k3-thompson (-.070), pg-actor untuned (-.005).
- Vs Thompson: every Hebbian-family config is better by +.08 to +.15 (30/30). The Thompson-led meshes are only +.02 to +.03.

ABLATIONS: each mesh vs its own bare leader (held-out)
- mesh-tuned vs hebbian-tuned: +.0185 [+.007, +.030]. Team tasks +.076; solo tasks -.006 (n.s.).
- mesh-trust-tuned vs hebbian-tuned: +.020 [+.007, +.033]. Failure window +.025 (significant); team tasks +.070.
- trust-mesh-tuned vs hebbian-tuned: +.024.
- mesh-k2 vs hebbian: +.026. mesh-k3 vs hebbian: +.023.
- mesh-k2-thompson vs thompson: +.030.
- mesh-tuned vs mesh-trust-tuned: -.002 (n.s.). mesh-tuned vs trust-mesh-tuned: -.006 (n.s.). The two edge rules perform the same.
- pg-actor-tuned vs hebbian-tuned: -.021 (significantly worse). r-stdp-tuned vs hebbian-tuned: +.001 (n.s.).

ROBUSTNESS CHECKS (held-out seeds)
- Task type revealed to routers:
  - Thompson rises to .736.
  - hebbian-tuned is then no better than Thompson (+.004, n.s.).
  - mesh-tuned (+.027), mesh-k2/k3-thompson (+.028), trust-mesh-tuned (+.021) and r-stdp-tuned (+.014) still beat Thompson significantly.
  - So the large margins over Thompson in the main run come from the baseline keying only on the first (shuffled) keyword.
- Reward delayed by 25 tasks (lead's request):
  - mesh-tuned .741 and trust-mesh-tuned .737 still beat keyword and hebbian-tuned (+.02, significant).
  - R-STDP's eligibility trace gives no advantage (.7185 vs hebbian-tuned .7171, n.s.).
  - Default hebbian and mesh-k1 fall significantly below keyword.

WHERE THE MESH DOES NOT HELP
- Solo tasks: no gain anywhere. Adding teams slightly hurts solo tasks (mesh-tuned vs mesh-tuned-k1 on solo: -.013, significant).
- Health/benching alone: mesh-k1 equals hebbian (n.s.). mesh-tuned-k1 only helps inside the failure window (+.014), not overall (n.s.).
- Untuned meshes: mesh-k2-trust and mesh-k3-trust do not beat keyword.
- Team size 3 never beats team size 2 for the co-activation mesh.
- Untuned Hebbian does not beat keyword, so every win depends on tuning.
- Cost: on team tasks the mesh uses 2-3 agent calls instead of 1. Routing takes about 0.9-1.2 µs per call, against 0.13 µs for keyword and about 0.6 µs for Hebbian alone.

VERDICT
By the DESIGN.md rule (95% CI over 30 seeds excludes 0, all tests pass), tuned Hebbian and all tuned meshes pass against both baselines on held-out seeds. What the mesh adds over its own leader is about +2 points overall, all of it from teaming on team tasks. Health benching only shows a small effect inside the failure window. The co-activation and trust edge rules are statistically the same. PgActor and R-STDP do not beat tuned Hebbian, including with delayed reward.

Caveats:
- The wins depend on tuning.
- The margin over Thompson depends on hiding the task type.
- The team-task gain depends on this sim's synergy model, where 3 of 15 pairs are strongly synergistic.

Present it as a modest, conditional win.
